artists.biography:
Matthew Charles "Matt" Berry (born 2 May 1974) is an English actor, writer, comedian and musician. Berry is perhaps best known for his appearances in The IT Crowd, Garth Marenghi's Darkplace, The Mighty Boosh, and Snuff Box. He is renowned for his deep voice; he has voiced several advertisements, most notably for Volvic, The Natural Confectionery Company, Absolute Radio, and MoneySupermarket.

As a musician, Berry composed all the music for Snuff Box, as well as the music for AD/BC: A Rock Opera, which he co-wrote with Richard Ayoade. AD/BC was a half-hour parody of overblown musicals in general and Jesus Christ Superstar in particular, telling the story of the innkeeper who allowed Mary, Joseph, and the baby Jesus to sleep in his manger. AD/BC was broadcast in December 2004 and featured Fulcher and Mighty Boosh stars Julian Barratt and Noel Fielding. He also performed a song for an episode of Garth Marenghi's Darkplace entitled "One Track Lover", a spoof of cheesy romantic 80s songs.

perplexity.description:
Heard Noises," released on January 24, 2025, is the eleventh studio album by English musician Matt Berry, issued through Acid Jazz Records. The album marks a return to vocal-driven music for Berry, following his 2023 instrumental release Simplicity and his previous vocal studio album The Blue Elephant (2021). Musically, it blends rock with elements of neo-psychedelia and pop/rock, showcasing Berry's multi-instrumental talents and a rich, layered production style that incorporates vintage keyboards and synthesizers alongside traditional rock instrumentation.

The album features collaborations with notable artists such as Eric D. Johnson and Kitty Liv, contributing to its diverse sonic palette. Critically, Heard Noises was met with universal acclaim, receiving an average score of 84 on Metacritic. Reviewers highlighted it as one of Berry's strongest works, with AllMusic's Tim Sendra placing it near the top of Berry's discography and praising its vibrant, sunlit soundscapes. This positive reception underscores the album's significance as a mature, confident statement in Berry's evolving career.
